Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **SVG vector images** on KAG and World layers, on every platform: `[image layer=0 storage=emblem.svg]` or `[newlay name=badge file=emblem show]`. The layerExVector plugin draws them again at each zoom and angle, so they stay sharp where a bitmap blurs. A name without an extension finds an SVG when no bitmap has that name. SVG text isn't drawn: convert it to outlines in the drawing program
- The sample's KAGEX Extended Layer demo ends with an SVG emblem beside a PNG of the same picture, both zoomed and turned
- The Android and iOS builds now include layerExVector, as the desktop and web builds did
- `.emf` and `.wmf` images still need GDI+ (the Windows-only engine); on the SDL engine they now say so and suggest SVG
- kagex-release 0.6.0 downloads the 0.6.0 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.6.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
